what_this_overlay_does_not_mean: NOT a change to any route's historical publication_ready or publication_condition value. Those fields are read here and are written nowhere.
NOT permission to index. Staging noindex protections are retained in full and are asserted by test.

NOT, by itself, authorization to deploy anything. This overlay records readiness; deployment is authorized separately and is carried out by Git Commander. Staging was subsequently activated under that later authority and STAGING = ACTIVE; PRODUCTION = LOCKED.
NOT a statement that these routes are ready to publish. Staging readiness and publication readiness are different questions and this overlay answers only the first.
NOT permission to submit to the production Typeform form.

historical_authority_preserved.rule: The historical frozen fields are read, never written, and never reinterpreted. This overlay is a SECOND and SEPARATE reading that answers a different question.
historical_authority_preserved.PUBLIC_ROUTE_REGISTRY.tsv#publication_re: NOT_READY_CONTENT_REMEDIATION_INCOMPLETE on all 29 cohort rows - unchanged, still the authority for publication and indexing

the_two_questions.is_this_route_published_and_indexable: answered ONLY by the historical publication_ready / publication_condition fields. Answer today: NO, for all 29.
the_two_questions.may_the_accepted_typeform_interface_be_e: answered by this overlay. Answer today: YES, for all 29.

protections_retained: PAGE_ROBOTS_NOINDEX: every route's page metadata continues to read the historical publication gate and continues to emit noindex, nofollow.
X_ROBOTS_TAG_NOINDEX: the response header continues to read the same historical gate on all 29 routes.
PRIVATE_PREVIEW_NOTICE: continues to render on every route, bound to the historical gate.
NAVIGATION_LABEL_SUPPRESSION: navigation labels continue to be decided by the historical gate. Navigation is accepted and is not reopened by this overlay.

PRODUCTION_LOCKED: unchanged. Production deployment and DNS remain locked. Staging is ACTIVE under later authority; the noindex, nofollow and private-preview protections listed above apply to it in full and are asserted by test.

staging_readiness.applies_to: the 29 accepted launch-cohort routes, enumerated below and required to equal the cohort exactly

mounts_added.label: Request a Quote
mounts_added.rationale: The owner's V1 conversion UX: a persistent site-wide affordance that opens the accepted conversational Typeform dialog. It introduces no chatbot, no chat-form engine, no CRM, no Revenue Engine, no native RFQ persistence and no custom email handling. Typeform remains the form and notification engine.
mounts_added.precedence: LOWEST. The launcher renders in a neutral treatment whenever a higher-precedence signal-colour action exists on the route, so the accepted single-signal-action rule is preserved.

mounts_added.label: Request a Quote
mounts_added.rationale: The homepage hero is the estate's first conversion decision point, and the accepted contract carries no in-body mount for a COMPANY_OR_SERVICE route. This adds one, on the homepage only, through the accepted adapter. It renders in the neutral treatment because header_action outranks it, so the accepted single-signal-action rule is unchanged; the hero control reads as primary through scale, not colour.

mounts_added.label: Request a Quote
mounts_added.rationale: The accepted homepage body carries its own 'Request a quote' section. This mount places the accepted interface at that accepted decision point instead of leaving the section as prose with no action. Neutral treatment, same reason as above.

mounts_added.label: Request a Quote
mounts_added.rationale: The accepted contract mounts editorial_inline on the 22 editorial routes and rfq_page on /contact-us/, which leaves the five other commercial routes with no in-page conversion action at all: a reader on the thermal upgrade page or the parts catalogue had to return to the header. This adds one, on those five routes only, through the accepted adapter. Neutral treatment, so the single signal-colour action per viewport remains header_action.

mount_pattern_decisions.reason: No accepted authority supplies an embedded-in-page RFQ surface, and the accepted Phase 2C-min R1.1 adapter supplies only the QuoteCta dialog interface. Rather than fabricate a new embedded implementation or leave the Contact page with no conversion path, V1 opens the same accepted conversational Typeform dialog from the Contact page. The historical EMBEDDED_IN_PAGE intent is preserved above and is not deleted.
mount_pattern_decisions.deferred: The embedded-in-page surface, and the future custom CRM / chat-form architecture, remain deferred and unauthorised.

viewport_precedence_addition.rule: The accepted rule is unchanged: exactly one signal-colour RFQ action may be visible in any viewport at any time. floating_quote_launcher is appended at the END of the accepted precedence order, so it never displaces an accepted mount and never becomes a second signal-colour action. R2 adds two homepage mounts to that same order, after the accepted eight and before floating_quote_launcher, for the same reason: both render in the neutral treatment, so the single signal-colour action on the homepage remains the accepted header_action.
viewport_precedence_addition.note: R2: the two homepage mounts are inserted after the accepted eight and before floating_quote_launcher, so both properties R1 asserted still hold — the accepted order is an unmodified prefix, and the persistent launcher remains last and therefore can never displace another mount’s treatment.

typeform_configuration.required_for_real_dialog_validation: A NON-PRODUCTION Typeform form id, supplied externally. Not present in any accepted input. NOT INVENTED HERE.
typeform_configuration.rule: No test submission is sent into the production lead flow. No form id, origin, notification recipient or analytics destination is invented, proposed or changed by this overlay.

not_authorised_by_this_overlay: Git commit, push, branch or pull request
Staging deployment, production deployment or DNS
Any Payload, database or media mutation
Any Typeform account, workspace or form change
Any live or test submission to the production form
A custom CRM, Revenue Engine, chatbot, chat-form backend, SMTP/email infrastructure or native RFQ persistence
Any change to indexing, robots direction, navigation, media, accepted content or design
revision_note: R2 extends the R1 overlay for the authorized real-staging visual implementation. It adds two homepage in-page conversion mounts and nothing else. Every protection R1 retained is retained here unchanged, verbatim. No historical authority, route, canonical, robots direction or media selection is touched.

staging_navigation_authorization.authorized_by: Control Tower directive H2O FULL CONTENT + MEDIA RECOVERY + REAL-STAGING VISUAL R2, section 23 'NAVIGATION - BOUNDED STAGING AUTHORIZATION'
staging_navigation_authorization.rule: On private staging a navigation label may render when, and only when, both hold: (1) its target is a canonical path of the accepted 29-route cohort, and (2) that route is READY_FOR_PRIVATE_STAGING_VALIDATION under this overlay. Both conditions are evaluated per request against the live cohort, never baked in.
what_this_does_not_change: publication_ready and publication_condition are untouched on all 29 rows and remain the sole authority for publication and indexing.

navTargetRenderable, the historical publication gate, is unchanged and still answers the publication question. This authorization adds a second, separate reading for staging navigation; it does not merge the two.
Staging remains noindex, nofollow at the proxy header and in page metadata, and the private-preview notice remains on all 29 routes.
Every navigation label whose target is outside the accepted cohort stays suppressed, exactly as before. No destination is invented and no label is repointed at a substitute page.
The accepted navigation contract file is read, never written. Its labels, targets and suppression instructions are unchanged.

measured_consequence.count_reconciliation: R2 reported nine renderable targets and enumerated seven. Both numbers are real and they count different things. Nine is the number of occurrences in the accepted navigation contract whose target is a canonical path of the 29-route cohort. Seven of those nine are navigation labels and render as navigation. The remaining two are conversion-path entries — the footer RFQ band action and the cta_semantics primary — which resolve to /contact-us/ and render as the request-a-quote call to action, not as a navigation label. No destination was invented to reconcile the numbers; the two additional occurrences were already in the contract and are now named.

staging_navigation_authorization.relationship_to_NAVIGATION_LABEL_SUPPRES: The protection R1 retained says navigation labels continue to be decided by the historical gate. That remains true of publication, which is the question that protection was about, and protections_retained is unchanged byte for byte. This entry is an addition beside it, authorized by name in the directive above, and it governs one thing: whether a label may render on a private, noindex staging host whose target route is in the accepted cohort and is staging-validation-ready.

deployment_state.what_active_means: A private preview host serves the cohort. It remains noindex, nofollow in page metadata and in the response header, and it continues to carry the private-preview notice on all 29 routes.
deployment_state.what_this_overlay_authorizes: Readiness only. This overlay alone does not authorize deployment to staging, to production or to DNS.
deployment_state.staging_readiness_is_not_publication_rea: A route being READY_FOR_PRIVATE_STAGING_VALIDATION says the accepted interface may be exercised behind the private preview. It says nothing about whether the route may be published or indexed; publication_ready and publication_condition remain the only authority for that, and they read NOT_READY on all 29 rows.
deployment_state.who_deploys: Git Commander owns all Git and deployment operations. The factory performs none.
deployment_state.correction_note: R1 and R2 of this overlay carried the line 'STAGING = LOCKED. PRODUCTION = LOCKED.' and 'STAGING_AND_PRODUCTION_LOCKED: unchanged.' Staging has since been activated under later authority, so that wording was stale and is corrected here. The protections_retained list is amended only at the one entry that stated the staging lock; every other entry in it is unchanged byte for byte.
